title: Growing up in the French Quarter among musicians, Danny Barker next door
summary: Albert names the Creole neighbourhood and the musicians who lived there, including Bigard, Manuel Perez, Piron, and Danny Barker across the street.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. To get back to your very earliest days, we're going to kind of jump around, but... What did you call the neighborhood you lived in? Where you grew up?

The French Quarters. It's all part of the French Quarters. The French Settlement in North Robeson, between Annette and St. Antony. In those days, it was spread out a little more than it is now. Mm-hmm. Go ahead. That's the section there where most of what they said are Creoles were living in. Mm-hmm. And... Bonnie was about a block from me. He was on... he was on Billerish Street. And we all... Manuel Perez was right on Earthquark Street. All of it was concentrated area there.
Mm-hmm. Lots of musicians in. Lots of musicians. Who were some of the other ones that you... What were the other ones that you...

Well, uh... Milford Piron, my teacher. Armand Piron. Thank you. Louis Cottrell's daddy. Bonnie Bigard, the Teos. Lorenzo Junior, Lorenzo Senior. Big I, Louis. Well, we could just go on and name quite a number of them. Piku.
The guys your age, how many of them are there? Let's see.
Well, quite a number of those that I mentioned were just a few years older than me. But the young ones would be like, uh, Cottrell. Bonnie.
Danny was raised with me right... right opposite each other's.
Other side of the street, huh?

Right on the other side of the street. We played in each other's yard. Mm-hmm. When we got mad with each other like kids would do, I'd put him out of my yard today. The next day he'd put me out of his yard. And he'd come back Saturday and Sunday. We were going around together helping his daddy pedal his charcoal and taking care of the horse and wagon. Yeah, Danny's been a beautiful friend of mine. Yeah. For years.
